FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Gaskets and Packings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, otied or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( rrcvimd )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified valw in this standard.

Indian Standard INSULATION MILL BOARD 1 SCOPE This standard covers insulation mill board having low contents asbestos fibres used for thermal insulation, acoustic insulation, electric insulation and for gaskets. 2 DIMENSIONS The length and width of the sheets shall be as agreed between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 2.1 The recommended nominal thicknesses insulation mill board are as follows: 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, lOand 125mm
NOTE - Insulation mill board can be manufactured in other thicknesses as agreed between the manufacturer and the purchaser.

3.1 Insulation mill board sheets shall be smooth, free from cracks, dents as well as foreign particles. The edges of the sheets should be evenly cut. 3.2 The quality characteristics of the insulation mill board, when tested at ambient temperature, shall meet the requirements specified in Table 1, 4 SAMPLING Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer, the sampling plan and criteria for conformity as given in 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 shall be followed. 4.1 Lot In any consignment all the sheets of same grade and dimensions manufactured under essentially similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 4.2 Material shall be submitted for acceptance in lots weighing not more than 3 000 kg including sheets of the same dimensions. 4.3 Three sheets shall be selected from a lot for carrying out the tests like thickness, chemical, physical and mechanical properties. 4.4 If any sample fails to comply with the requirements of any test other than dimensions, double the number of samples shall be selected from the same batch for retest and each of them shall comply with the requirement of that test. SMARKING 5.1 Each sheet shall be marked with the date of production, code and manufacturer's brand name. 5.2 BIS Certification Marking The product may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of Bureau oflndian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6 PACKING Insulation mill board sheet may be supplied flat, suitably packed to prevent damage as per the requirement of the purchaser. 7 TEST METHODS The selected sheets of insulation mill board shall be cut along mutually perpendicular directions into four equal parts rectangular in shape and then two of these parts located along the same diagonal shall be tested. 7.1 Conditioning All specimen shall be conditioned as described in Annex A before testing. 7.2 Dimensions The length and width of sheets shall bc checked with the aid of a metal tape/rule to the nearest 1 mm. The thickness of the sheets shall be determined with the aid of a dead weight micrometer with an anvil of 10 mm in diameter by measuring the thickness of two cut 2

parts of the sheet at four points along the perimeter of each part of the sheets. Measurements shall be taken to the nearest 0.1 mm and at a distance of not less than 20 mm from the edge of the sheet. The arithmetic mean of all the measurements shall be considered to be the thickness. 7.3 Density A test piece of 100 mm x 100 mm shall be weighed nearest to 0.1 g and its thickness ascertained according to 2.2. The mass oftest piece in g divided by its volume in cm' gives the density. 7.4 Tensile Strength The tensile strength shall be determined by the method described in Annex B. 7.5 Water Contents Test The water contents shall be determined by the method described in Annex C 7.6 Loss on Ignition Test The loss on ignition shall be determined by the method described in Annex D. 7.7 pH of Water Extract Test The pH of water extract shall be determined by the method described in Annex E. 7.8 Chloride and Sulphate Contents Test The chloride and sulphate contents in the water extract shall be determined by the method described in Annex F. 7.9 Fire Proofness Insulation mill board should not catch fire on burning the sheet in fire. 7.10 Compressibility and Recovery The compressibility and recovery shall be determined by the method described in Annex G. lnsulation mill board of 1.6 mm thickness shall be subjected to this test. For other thicknesses the test piccc shall be taken from 1.6 mm thick board guaranteed by the manufacturer to be of equivalent quality

ANNEX A (Clause 7.1 )
METHOD OF CONDlTIONlNG A-l The specimen shall be conditioned in an oven at 105'C to 1lO'C for 2 h and allowed to cool at room temperature for two to three hours in a desiccator containing anhydrous calcium chloride or silica gel.

ANNEX B ( Clause 7.4 )
METHOD OF DETERMINlNG TENSILE STRENGTH B-l Four test strips 300 mm long and 25 mm wide shall be cut or stamped from two parts of a sheet at a distance of at least 10 mm from the edge (two strips in mutually perpendicular .directions from each part of the sheet). The strip shall be free from mechanical damage. Each specimen shall be provided wit!1 an arrow indicating the direction in which the strip was cut. The test piece shall be conditioned as described in 7.1. B-2 The tensile strength shall be determinedby testing these strips in suitable tensile testing machine. The distance between the clamps shall be equal to 200 mm and the lower clamp shall move at a rate of 50 mm/ min. After testing specimen, the thickness and width of cross section should be measured by a micrometer/ thickness gauge. B-3 The tensile strength, s (kgf cm') shall bc determined as: P
S" /i

where P = Breaking load in kgf, and A = Cross-sectional area of specimen in cm'. B-4 The tensile strength of insulation mill board sheet for each direction shall be calculated as the arithmetic mean of the test results obtained on four strips.

ANNEX C ( Clause 7.5 )
METHOD OF DETERMINING WATER CONTEN'IS C-l A portion of insulation mill board weighing approx 10 g taken from two parts of each sheet (see 7) shall be placed in a previously weighed glass dish with glass cover and weighed to the nearest 0.01 g, dried in a thermostatically controlled air oven at a temperature of 105'C to 110�C for two hours, then cooled in a desiccator for one hour minimum and weighed with the same precision. Drying and weighing of the glass dish with weighed portion of the sheet shall be repeated until the results of two successive weighings do not differ by more than 0.0 1 g. C-2 Water contents percentage shall be calculated as: 3 CC' - w Water contents in percentage = $--$ x 100
1 R

where w, = Weight of glass dish with specimen in g before drying, w, = Weight of glass dish with specimen in g after drying, and w, = Weight of glass dish in g C-3 The arithmetic means of three test results shall be taken as the water contents of insulation mill board of the given lot.

ANNEX D ( Ckzuse 7.6 )
METHOD OF DETERMINING LOSS ON IGNITION D-l A portion of the dried sheet weighing approx 10 g taken after determination of water contents (see 7.9, shall be placed in a previously weighed crucible, weighed to the nearest 0.01 g and ignited in a muflle furnace at a temperature of 800 f 20�C for one hour. D-2 Ignition and weighing of the crucible with the weighed test piece shall be repeated until the results of two successive weighings do not differ by more thanO.O1 g. D-3 Loss on ignition in percent shall be calculated as: w-w Loss on ignition, in percentage = * where w, = Weight of crucible and test piece in g before ignition, x 100

D-4 The arithmetic means of these test results shall be taken as loss on ignition of insulation mill board of the given lot.

ANNEX E ( Clause 7.7 )
METHOD OF DETERMMN GpII OF WATER EXTRACT
E-l A portion of the insulation mill board weighing

15 g taken from two parts of each sheet shall be placed in a 500 ml conical ilask, then 300 ml of distilled water with apH ranging from 6.6 to 7.1 shall be poured into the flask. The contents of the flask shall be vigorously shaken, allowed to stand and shaken again after

30 min and then filtered through a clean glass porous filter. E-2 The first portion of the filtrate (20 to 30 ml) shall be discarded, then 100 to 200 ml filtrate (of the water extract) shall be collected and itspH is determined by quinhydrone method, using apH meter.

ANNEX F ( CZause 7.8 )
ME'I'IIOD OF DETERMINING CHLORIDE AND SULPIUTE CONTENTS F-l The presence of Cl and SO, in the water extract shall be determined in the filtrate remaining unused after the determination of pH (see 7.7). The water extract shall be poured into two clean glass test tubes. Several drops of concentrate nitric acid and then several drops of a one percent solution of silver nitrate shall be added to one of the test tubes. If after the addition of the reagents, the water extract in the test tube remains transparent (no formation of suspended matter is observed) this indicates that the water extract 4 is free from Cl F-2 Several drops of concentrated hydrochloric acid and then several drops of a heated 10 percent solution of barium chloride shall be added to the other test tube. After that, water extract shall be heated to boiling. If after the addition of the reagents the water extract in the test tube remains transparent (no formation of suspended matter is observed), this indicates that the water extract is free from SO,.

METHOD OF DETERMINATION OF COM.PRlfSDHLJTY AND RECOVERY G-l Three test pieces of square shape and have

minimum area of 6.5 cm* shall be cut or stamped from the sample and conditioned as described in 7.1. The conditioned test piece shall be tested for compressibility and recovery test on a suitable testing machine. The testing machine shall have a hardened and ground surface of 3 1.7 mm minimum diameter, a steel penetrator of 64 f 0.025 mm diameter with hardened and ground end and a dial gauge of 0.01 mm least count. G-2 A preload of 4.4 N shall be applied with no test specimen in place and record the dial gauge reading (r,). The procedure shall be repeated after placing the specimen centrally and the initial load is maintained for 15s. Record the dial gauge reading (T,) at this load. Then an additional load is applied immediately in slow uniformmannersothatatotalloadof218Nreachwithin 10 s. The total load is maintained for 60 s, and then record the dial gauge reading (TJ. Immediately remove the additional load and after a period of 60 s, record the dial gauge reading CT,) under the preload.

Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'.
